t2i_prompt: A 1440 px wide desktop web section as a top-down flat-lay photograph. A limestone surface with a deep navy panel along the right edge. Loosely arranged physical objects, one per item of <CONTENT>: kraft shipping tags with grommets, a round hang tag, manila and kraft folders with tabs and a metal paper clip, each printed with bold caps titles, typewriter monospace notes and large numbers. Small glass sample vials and ampoules as props, a rubber stamp mark, steel-blue label accents. Soft overhead lighting, gentle realistic shadows, visible paper grain.
signature_idea: Each optional module is a physical shipping tag or folder on a desk, as if options were packed and labelled for the build.
strengths: memorable and human, breaks the sequence of dark technical sections
tags and folders echo real paperwork and shipping of a skid
numbered items keep the option count clear
weaknesses: photo-real props and kraft paper are off-brand vs precise line art
heavy bold caps on tags fight Geist light
scattered layout hurts scanning and responsive translation
glass ampoules read as medicine vials, wrong product cue
fake UI toggles on paper confuse affordance
hard to reproduce as a token-only component
brand_fit_why: Navy/limestone and mono labels nod to the brand, but photo-real kraft props, bold caps and loose scatter break the precise, calm, flat, square-cornered system.
